heroHeadline: Trump-Xi Summit: Hormuz 'Must Remain Open', Iran 'Can Never Have Nuclear Weapon'; Vessel Seized Near Fujairah; Vance Says 'Progress' on Nuclear Talks — Day 76
heroSubtitle: Day 76 (May 14): Trump and Xi Jinping reached a landmark joint agreement in Beijing — the Strait of Hormuz 'must remain open' and Iran 'can never have a nuclear weapon,' according to a White House readout. Xi also voiced opposition to IRGC militarization of the strait and to Iran's toll-charging — a direct repudiation of the May 4 maritime control zone and May 13 geographic expansion. Xi expressed interest in buying more US oil to reduce China's own Hormuz dependence. VP Vance told reporters the US is 'making progress' on Iran nuclear talks, describing Trump's red line as ensuring Iran 'will never have a nuclear weapon.' Even as diplomacy advanced, UKMTO reported a commercial vessel seized by unknown personnel 38 nautical miles northeast of Fujairah, redirected toward Iranian waters — the 47th maritime incident since February 28. On Capitol Hill, 52 senators and 177 House members (every GOP senator except Rand Paul) sent Trump a letter demanding any deal require Iran to give up all uranium enrichment, including for civilian energy — a zero-enrichment demand. Israel and Lebanon opened a third round of Washington peace talks as the Lebanon-Israel ceasefire neared its May 17 expiry; Lebanon's toll stands at 2,896 killed. Netanyahu's office revealed he secretly visited UAE during the war, claiming a 'historic breakthrough'; UAE called the reports 'entirely unfounded.' Day 75 recap (May 13): Trump arrived in Beijing; IRGC declared maximum readiness with 'no room for retreat'; IRGC Navy announced vast Hormuz geographic expansion; Australia joined UK/France defensive Hormuz escort mission.
